title: מלכים א פרק 10

verses: וּמַלְכַּת-שְׁבָא, שֹׁמַעַת אֶת-שֵׁמַע שְׁלֹמֹה--לְשֵׁם יְהוָה; וַתָּבֹא לְנַסֹּתוֹ, בְּחִידוֹת.
וַתָּבֹא יְרוּשָׁלְַמָה, בְּחַיִל כָּבֵד מְאֹד, גְּמַלִּים נֹשְׂאִים בְּשָׂמִים וְזָהָב רַב-מְאֹד, וְאֶבֶן יְקָרָה; וַתָּבֹא, אֶל-שְׁלֹמֹה, וַתְּדַבֵּר אֵלָיו, אֵת כָּל-אֲשֶׁר הָיָה עִם-לְבָבָהּ.
וַיַּגֶּד-לָהּ שְׁלֹמֹה, אֶת-כָּל-דְּבָרֶיהָ: לֹא-הָיָה דָבָר נֶעְלָם מִן-הַמֶּלֶךְ, אֲשֶׁר לֹא הִגִּיד לָהּ.
וַתֵּרֶא, מַלְכַּת-שְׁבָא, אֵת, כָּל-חָכְמַת שְׁלֹמֹה; וְהַבַּיִת, אֲשֶׁר בָּנָה.
וּמַאֲכַל שֻׁלְחָנוֹ וּמוֹשַׁב עֲבָדָיו וּמַעֲמַד מְשָׁרְתָו וּמַלְבֻּשֵׁיהֶם, וּמַשְׁקָיו, וְעֹלָתוֹ, אֲשֶׁר יַעֲלֶה בֵּית יְהוָה; וְלֹא-הָיָה בָהּ עוֹד, רוּחַ.
וַתֹּאמֶר, אֶל-הַמֶּלֶךְ, אֱמֶת הָיָה הַדָּבָר, אֲשֶׁר שָׁמַעְתִּי בְּאַרְצִי--עַל-דְּבָרֶיךָ, וְעַל-חָכְמָתֶךָ.
וְלֹא-הֶאֱמַנְתִּי לַדְּבָרִים, עַד אֲשֶׁר-בָּאתִי וַתִּרְאֶינָה עֵינַי, וְהִנֵּה לֹא-הֻגַּד-לִי, הַחֵצִי: הוֹסַפְתָּ חָכְמָה וָטוֹב, אֶל-הַשְּׁמוּעָה אֲשֶׁר שָׁמָעְתִּי.
אַשְׁרֵי אֲנָשֶׁיךָ, אַשְׁרֵי עֲבָדֶיךָ אֵלֶּה, הָעֹמְדִים לְפָנֶיךָ תָּמִיד, הַשֹּׁמְעִים אֶת-חָכְמָתֶךָ.
יְהִי יְהוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ, בָּרוּךְ, אֲשֶׁר חָפֵץ בְּךָ, לְתִתְּךָ עַל-כִּסֵּא יִשְׂרָאֵל--בְּאַהֲבַת יְהוָה אֶת-יִשְׂרָאֵל, לְעֹלָם, וַיְשִׂימְךָ לְמֶלֶךְ, לַעֲשׂוֹת מִשְׁפָּט וּצְדָקָה.
וַתִּתֵּן לַמֶּלֶךְ מֵאָה וְעֶשְׂרִים כִּכַּר זָהָב, וּבְשָׂמִים הַרְבֵּה מְאֹד--וְאֶבֶן יְקָרָה; לֹא בָא כַבֹּשֶׂם הַהוּא עוֹד לָרֹב, אֲשֶׁר-נָתְנָה מַלְכַּת-שְׁבָא לַמֶּלֶךְ שְׁלֹמֹה.
וְגַם אֳנִי חִירָם, אֲשֶׁר-נָשָׂא זָהָב מֵאוֹפִיר: הֵבִיא מֵאֹפִיר עֲצֵי אַלְמֻגִּים, הַרְבֵּה מְאֹד--וְאֶבֶן יְקָרָה.
וַיַּעַשׂ הַמֶּלֶךְ אֶת-עֲצֵי הָאַלְמֻגִּים מִסְעָד לְבֵית-יְהוָה, וּלְבֵית הַמֶּלֶךְ, וְכִנֹּרוֹת וּנְבָלִים, לַשָּׁרִים; לֹא בָא-כֵן עֲצֵי אַלְמֻגִּים, וְלֹא נִרְאָה, עַד, הַיּוֹם הַזֶּה.
וְהַמֶּלֶךְ שְׁלֹמֹה נָתַן לְמַלְכַּת-שְׁבָא, אֶת-כָּל-חֶפְצָהּ אֲשֶׁר שָׁאָלָה, מִלְּבַד אֲשֶׁר נָתַן-לָהּ, כְּיַד הַמֶּלֶךְ שְׁלֹמֹה; וַתֵּפֶן וַתֵּלֶךְ לְאַרְצָהּ, הִיא וַעֲבָדֶיהָ.
וַיְהִי מִשְׁקַל הַזָּהָב, אֲשֶׁר-בָּא לִשְׁלֹמֹה בְּשָׁנָה אֶחָת--שֵׁשׁ מֵאוֹת שִׁשִּׁים וָשֵׁשׁ, כִּכַּר זָהָב.
לְבַד מֵאַנְשֵׁי הַתָּרִים, וּמִסְחַר הָרֹכְלִים, וְכָל-מַלְכֵי הָעֶרֶב, וּפַחוֹת הָאָרֶץ.
וַיַּעַשׂ הַמֶּלֶךְ שְׁלֹמֹה מָאתַיִם צִנָּה, זָהָב שָׁחוּט; שֵׁשׁ-מֵאוֹת זָהָב, יַעֲלֶה עַל-הַצִּנָּה הָאֶחָת.
וּשְׁלֹשׁ-מֵאוֹת מָגִנִּים, זָהָב שָׁחוּט--שְׁלֹשֶׁת מָנִים זָהָב, יַעֲלֶה עַל-הַמָּגֵן הָאֶחָת; וַיִּתְּנֵם הַמֶּלֶךְ, בֵּית יַעַר הַלְּבָנוֹן.
וַיַּעַשׂ הַמֶּלֶךְ כִּסֵּא-שֵׁן, גָּדוֹל; וַיְצַפֵּהוּ, זָהָב מוּפָז.
שֵׁשׁ מַעֲלוֹת לַכִּסֵּה, וְרֹאשׁ-עָגֹל לַכִּסֵּה מֵאַחֲרָיו, וְיָדֹת מִזֶּה וּמִזֶּה, אֶל-מְקוֹם הַשָּׁבֶת; וּשְׁנַיִם אֲרָיוֹת, עֹמְדִים אֵצֶל הַיָּדוֹת.
וּשְׁנֵים עָשָׂר אֲרָיִים, עֹמְדִים שָׁם עַל-שֵׁשׁ הַמַּעֲלוֹת--מִזֶּה וּמִזֶּה; לֹא-נַעֲשָׂה כֵן, לְכָל-מַמְלָכוֹת.
וְכֹל כְּלֵי מַשְׁקֵה הַמֶּלֶךְ שְׁלֹמֹה, זָהָב, וְכֹל כְּלֵי בֵּית-יַעַר הַלְּבָנוֹן, זָהָב סָגוּר: אֵין כֶּסֶף, לֹא נֶחְשָׁב בִּימֵי שְׁלֹמֹה--לִמְאוּמָה.
כִּי אֳנִי תַרְשִׁישׁ לַמֶּלֶךְ בַּיָּם, עִם אֳנִי חִירָם; אַחַת לְשָׁלֹשׁ שָׁנִים תָּבוֹא אֳנִי תַרְשִׁישׁ, נֹשְׂאֵת זָהָב וָכֶסֶף, שֶׁנְהַבִּים וְקֹפִים, וְתֻכִּיִּים.
וַיִּגְדַּל הַמֶּלֶךְ שְׁלֹמֹה, מִכֹּל מַלְכֵי הָאָרֶץ--לְעֹשֶׁר, וּלְחָכְמָה.
וְכָל-הָאָרֶץ--מְבַקְשִׁים, אֶת-פְּנֵי שְׁלֹמֹה: לִשְׁמֹעַ, אֶת-חָכְמָתוֹ, אֲשֶׁר-נָתַן אֱלֹהִים, בְּלִבּוֹ.
וְהֵמָּה מְבִאִים אִישׁ מִנְחָתוֹ כְּלֵי כֶסֶף וּכְלֵי זָהָב וּשְׂלָמוֹת, וְנֵשֶׁק וּבְשָׂמִים, סוּסִים, וּפְרָדִים--דְּבַר-שָׁנָה, בְּשָׁנָה.
וַיֶּאֱסֹף שְׁלֹמֹה, רֶכֶב וּפָרָשִׁים, וַיְהִי-לוֹ אֶלֶף וְאַרְבַּע-מֵאוֹת רֶכֶב, וּשְׁנֵים-עָשָׂר אֶלֶף פָּרָשִׁים; וַיַּנְחֵם בְּעָרֵי הָרֶכֶב, וְעִם-הַמֶּלֶךְ בִּירוּשָׁלִָם.
וַיִּתֵּן הַמֶּלֶךְ אֶת-הַכֶּסֶף בִּירוּשָׁלִַם, כָּאֲבָנִים; וְאֵת הָאֲרָזִים, נָתַן כַּשִּׁקְמִים אֲשֶׁר-בַּשְּׁפֵלָה--לָרֹב.
וּמוֹצָא הַסּוּסִים אֲשֶׁר לִשְׁלֹמֹה, מִמִּצְרָיִם; וּמִקְוֵה--סֹחֲרֵי הַמֶּלֶךְ, יִקְחוּ מִקְוֵה בִּמְחִיר.
וַתַּעֲלֶה וַתֵּצֵא מֶרְכָּבָה מִמִּצְרַיִם, בְּשֵׁשׁ מֵאוֹת כֶּסֶף, וְסוּס, בַּחֲמִשִּׁים וּמֵאָה; וְכֵן לְכָל-מַלְכֵי הַחִתִּים, וּלְמַלְכֵי אֲרָם--בְּיָדָם יֹצִאוּ.
english: And when the queen of Sheba heard of the fame of Solomon concerning the name of the Lord, she came to prove him with hard questions.

And she came to Jerusalem with a very great train, with camels that bare spices, and very much gold, and precious stones: and when she was come to Solomon, she communed with him of all that was in her heart.
And Solomon told her all her questions: there was not any thing hid from the king, which he told her not.
And when the queen of Sheba had seen all Solomon's wisdom, and the house that he had built,

And the meat of his table, and the sitting of his servants, and the attendance of his ministers, and their apparel, and his cupbearers, and his ascent by which he went up unto the house of the Lord; there was no more spirit in her.
And she said to the king, It was a true report that I heard in mine own land of thy acts and of thy wisdom.
Howbeit I believed not the words, until I came, and mine eyes had seen it: and, behold, the half was not told me: thy wisdom and prosperity exceedeth the fame which I heard.
Happy are thy men, happy are these thy servants, which stand continually before thee, and that hear thy wisdom.
Blessed be the Lord thy God, which delighted in thee, to set thee on the throne of Israel: because the Lord loved Israel for ever, therefore made he thee king, to do judgment and justice.

And she gave the king an hundred and twenty talents of gold, and of spices very great store, and precious stones: there came no more such abundance of spices as these which the queen of Sheba gave to king Solomon.
And the navy also of Hiram, that brought gold from Ophir, brought in from Ophir great plenty of almug trees, and precious stones.
And the king made of the almug trees pillars for the house of the Lord, and for the king's house, harps also and psalteries for singers: there came no such almug trees, nor were seen unto this day.

And king Solomon gave unto the queen of Sheba all her desire, whatsoever she asked, beside that which Solomon gave her of his royal bounty. So she turned and went to her own country, she and her servants.
Now the weight of gold that came to Solomon in one year was six hundred threescore and six talents of gold,
Beside that he had of the merchantmen, and of the traffick of the spice merchants, and of all the kings of Arabia, and of the governors of the country.
And king Solomon made two hundred targets of beaten gold: six hundred shekels of gold went to one target.
And he made three hundred shields of beaten gold; three pound of gold went to one shield: and the king put them in the house of the forest of Lebanon.
Moreover the king made a great throne of ivory, and overlaid it with the best gold.
The throne had six steps, and the top of the throne was round behind: and there were stays on either side on the place of the seat, and two lions stood beside the stays.
And twelve lions stood there on the one side and on the other upon the six steps: there was not the like made in any kingdom.

And all king Solomon's drinking vessels were of gold, and all the vessels of the house of the forest of Lebanon were of pure gold; none were of silver: it was nothing accounted of in the days of Solomon.
For the king had at sea a navy of Tharshish with the navy of Hiram: once in three years came the navy of Tharshish, bringing gold, and silver, ivory, and apes, and peacocks.
So king Solomon exceeded all the kings of the earth for riches and for wisdom.
And all the earth sought to Solomon, to hear his wisdom, which God had put in his heart.
And they brought every man his present, vessels of silver, and vessels of gold, and garments, and armour, and spices, horses, and mules, a rate year by year.

And Solomon gathered together chariots and horsemen: and he had a thousand and four hundred chariots, and twelve thousand horsemen, whom he bestowed in the cities for chariots, and with the king at Jerusalem.
And the king made silver to be in Jerusalem as stones, and cedars made he to be as the sycomore trees that are in the vale, for abundance.
And Solomon had horses brought out of Egypt, and linen yarn: the king's merchants received the linen yarn at a price.

And a chariot came up and went out of Egypt for six hundred shekels of silver, and an horse for an hundred and fifty: and so for all the kings of the Hittites, and for the kings of Syria, did they bring them out by their means.
steinsaltz: וּמַלְכַּת־שְׁבָא שֹׁמַעַת אֶת־שֵׁמַע שְׁלֹמֹה. ייתכן ששבא שכנה בדרום ערב, בסביבות תימן או באפריקה המזרחית, אולי באתיופיה, לְשֵׁם ה'. שלמה היה מפורסם בכל העמים כגדול החכמים, וכמי שחכמתו חכמה אלוקית, ועל כן – וַתָּבֹא לְנַסֹּתוֹ בְּחִידוֹת, לשאול אותו שאלות, ולשמוע את תשובותיו החכמות. מלכת שבא לא ערכה את המסע למטרות פוליטיות, אלא בעיקר כדי להיפגש עם האיש ששמע חכמתו הגיע עד אליה.

וַתָּבֹא יְרוּשָׁלְַמָה בְּחַיִל כָּבֵד מְאֹד, גְּמַלִּים נֹשְׂאִים בְּשָׂמִים וְזָהָב רַב־מְאֹד וְאֶבֶן יְקָרָה. וַתָּבֹא אֶל־שְׁלֹמֹה, וַתְּדַבֵּר אֵלָיו אֵת כָּל־אֲשֶׁר הָיָה עִם־לְבָבָהּ. גְּמַלִּים נֹשְׂאִים בְּשָׂמִים וְזָהָב רַב־מְאֹד וְאֶבֶן יְקָרָה. וַתָּבֹא אֶל־שְׁלֹמֹה, וַתְּדַבֵּר אֵלָיו אֵת כָּל־אֲשֶׁר הָיָה עִם־לְבָבָהּ.
וַיַּגֶּד־לָהּ שְׁלֹמֹה אֶת־כָּל־דְּבָרֶיהָ, ענה על כל שאלותיה. לֹא־הָיָה דָבָר נֶעְלָם מִן־הַמֶּלֶךְ אֲשֶׁר לֹא הִגִּיד לָהּ.
וַתֵּרֶא מַלְכַּת־שְׁבָא אֵת כָּל־חָכְמַת שְׁלֹמֹה וְגם את הַבַּיִת אֲשֶׁר בָּנָה,

וּמַאֲכַל שֻׁלְחָנוֹ וּמוֹשַׁב עֲבָדָיו וּמַעֲמַד מְשָׁרְתָו וּמַלְבֻּשֵׁיהֶם וּמַשְׁקָיו וְעֹלָתוֹ אֲשֶׁר יַעֲלֶה, גרם המדרגות המפואר שהוביל מבית המלך עד בֵּית ה'. וְלֹא־הָיָה בָהּ עוֹד רוּחַ. היא נדהמה ביותר.
וַתֹּאמֶר אֶל־הַמֶּלֶךְ: אֱמֶת הָיָה הַדָּבָר אֲשֶׁר שָׁמַעְתִּי בְּאַרְצִי עַל־דְּבָרֶיךָ וְעַל־חָכְמָתֶךָ.

ai_explanation_en: The Queen of Sheba, who may have lived in southern Arabia around Yemen, in East Africa, or in Ethiopia, heard about Solomon’s wisdom and its divine character. She came to ask him questions and test his wisdom with riddles, mainly in order to meet the man whose wisdom had become known to her.
The Queen of Sheba arrived in Jerusalem with a very large caravan of camels carrying spices, much gold, and precious stones. She told Solomon all the questions and matters that concerned her.
Solomon answered all her questions, and nothing was hidden from him that he could not explain to her.
The Queen of Sheba saw Solomon’s wisdom and the house he had built.

She saw the food at his table, the seating of his servants, the order and appearance of his attendants, their clothing, his beverages, and the splendid staircase leading from the royal palace to the House of the Lord. She was overwhelmed with amazement.
She told the king that everything she had heard in her land about his words and wisdom was true.

She had not believed the reports until she came and saw with her own eyes. In her words, she had not even been told half of what she found, and Solomon had added wisdom and goodness beyond the report she had heard.
She praised Solomon’s people and servants, who were always able to stand before him and hear his wisdom, whereas she had only been able to have a few conversations with him.
She blessed the Lord, Solomon’s God, who had chosen him and placed him on Israel’s throne out of His love for Israel. Solomon’s task was to administer justice and righteousness.
The Queen of Sheba gave Solomon one hundred and twenty talents of gold, very large quantities of spices, and precious stones. No similar quantity of spices ever again arrived in Jerusalem.

At that time, additional treasures also arrived from the south through Hiram’s fleet, which brought gold from Ophir, algum wood or special trees from that region, and precious stones. According to the commentary, the value of the wood or coral was high because of its rarity and the distance from which it was brought.

Solomon used the algum wood, or the special trees, for railings in the House of the Lord and the royal palace, and also to make lyres and harps for the singers. Such a quantity of the wood had never been seen before, and its arrival was made possible by Solomon’s fleet.
Solomon gave the Queen of Sheba everything she requested, in addition to the gifts he generously gave her as befitted a king. She then returned to her land with her servants.
In one year, gold weighing six hundred and sixty-six talents came to Solomon. The year described was the year in which the Queen of Sheba arrived and gold also came on the Sidonian ships.
This total did not include the taxes brought by the trading caravans, traveling merchants, small-scale traders, the kings of Arabia, and the governors, meaning the officials of the land.

Solomon made two hundred large shields, or large defensive shields, from beaten gold. Each shield received six hundred gold coins, whose total weight was close to seven kilograms; “beaten gold” is explained as stretched gold or gold containing so few impurities that they changed its color.

He also made three hundred smaller shields of beaten gold. Each shield received three minas, a unit of weight equal to one hundred gold coins, and he placed the shields in the House of the Forest of Lebanon as a weapons store, a treasury, or for decoration.

Solomon made a large throne of ivory, meaning elephant tusk, and overlaid it with refined gold. “Mupaz” may mean gold from the distant place called Uphaz, or gold purified through pounding and scattering.
The throne had six steps, and behind it was a rounded back or ornament. There were handles on both sides for resting the hands, and two lion statues, probably made of gold, stood beside them.
Twelve lions stood on the six steps, one on each side of every step. No other kingdom had made such a throne.
All Solomon’s drinking vessels and all the vessels of the House of the Forest of Lebanon were made of refined gold. Because gold was so abundant, silver was not considered valuable in Solomon’s days.

Solomon’s fleet sailed on the sea with Hiram’s ships. Once every three years, large and powerful ships, capable of sailing as far as Tarshish, arrived carrying gold, silver, ivory, apes, and parrots, identified here with peacocks.
Solomon became greater than all the kings of the earth in wealth and wisdom.

The whole world sought an audience with Solomon in order to hear the wisdom that God had placed in his heart. The trade and long-distance connections contributed to the prosperity and renown described here.
The visitors brought Solomon personal gifts: silver and gold vessels, clothing, weapons, spices, horses, and mules. In this way, great treasures accumulated for Solomon year after year.

Solomon gathered chariots and horsemen, and he had one thousand four hundred chariots and twelve thousand horsemen. Some were stationed in the chariot cities for organization and protection against robbery, while others stayed with the king in Jerusalem.
Silver was abundant in Jerusalem, like stones. The cedars brought to Jerusalem were also so numerous that they were considered like the common sycamores of the lowlands.
Solomon’s horses came from Egypt. The king’s merchants gathered the horses there, and Solomon controlled the right to sell them and offered them to buyers at a price.

A chariot exported from Egypt was sold for six hundred pieces of silver, and a horse for one hundred and fifty. Chariots and horses were sold at the same price to the kings of the Hittites and the kings of Aram; Solomon bought the horses in Egypt, trained them, and sold them to the northern lands.

did_you_know.text_he: הידעת? מלכת שבא הגיעה לירושלים בחיל כבד, עם גמלים שנשאו בשמים, זהב רב ואבנים יקרות.
did_you_know.text_en: Did you know? The Queen of Sheba came to Jerusalem with a large entourage, including camels carrying spices, great quantities of gold, and precious stones.

did_you_know.text: הידעת? שלמה השיב על כל שאלותיה של מלכת שבא, והכתוב מדגיש שלא היה דבר נעלם ממנו שלא הגיד לה.
did_you_know.text_he: הידעת? שלמה השיב על כל שאלותיה של מלכת שבא, והכתוב מדגיש שלא היה דבר נעלם ממנו שלא הגיד לה.
did_you_know.text_en: Did you know? Solomon answered all the Queen of Sheba’s questions, and the text emphasizes that nothing was hidden from him that he could not explain to her.

did_you_know.text: הידעת? מלכת שבא לא התרשמה רק מחכמת שלמה, אלא גם ממאכל שולחנו, ממושב עבדיו, מסדר משרתיו, מלבושיהם, ממשקיו ומהעולה שהעלה בבית ה'.
did_you_know.text_he: הידעת? מלכת שבא לא התרשמה רק מחכמת שלמה, אלא גם ממאכל שולחנו, ממושב עבדיו, מסדר משרתיו, מלבושיהם, ממשקיו ומהעולה שהעלה בבית ה'.
did_you_know.text_en: Did you know? The Queen of Sheba was impressed not only by Solomon’s wisdom, but also by the food at his table, the seating of his servants, the order of his attendants, their clothing, his cupbearers, and the burnt offerings he presented at the house of the Lord.

did_you_know.text: הידעת? מלכת שבא קישרה בין מלכות שלמה לבין אהבת ה' לישראל, ושיבחה אותו על כך שהוא עושה משפט וצדקה.
did_you_know.text_he: הידעת? מלכת שבא קישרה בין מלכות שלמה לבין אהבת ה' לישראל, ושיבחה אותו על כך שהוא עושה משפט וצדקה.
did_you_know.text_en: Did you know? The Queen of Sheba connected Solomon’s kingdom with the Lord’s love for Israel and praised him for practicing justice and righteousness.

did_you_know.text: הידעת? מלכת שבא העניקה לשלמה מאה ועשרים כיכר זהב, בשמים רבים מאוד ואבנים יקרות.
did_you_know.text_he: הידעת? מלכת שבא העניקה לשלמה מאה ועשרים כיכר זהב, בשמים רבים מאוד ואבנים יקרות.
did_you_know.text_en: Did you know? The Queen of Sheba gave Solomon 120 talents of gold, a very large quantity of spices, and precious stones.

did_you_know.text: הידעת? עצי האלמוגים שהביא חירם מאופיר שימשו להכנת מסעדות לבית ה', לבית המלך וכלי נגינה למשוררים; הכתוב מציין שלא נראו עצים כאלה עד אותו היום.
did_you_know.text_he: הידעת? עצי האלמוגים שהביא חירם מאופיר שימשו להכנת מסעדות לבית ה', לבית המלך וכלי נגינה למשוררים; הכתוב מציין שלא נראו עצים כאלה עד אותו היום.
did_you_know.text_en: Did you know? The algum wood that Hiram brought from Ophir was used to make supports for the house of the Lord and the royal palace, as well as musical instruments for the singers; the text notes that no such wood had been seen until that day.

did_you_know.text: הידעת? משקל הזהב שהגיע לשלמה בשנה אחת היה שש מאות שישים ושש כיכר זהב, מלבד הכנסות נוספות מסוחרים, מלכים ופחות הארץ.
did_you_know.text_he: הידעת? משקל הזהב שהגיע לשלמה בשנה אחת היה שש מאות שישים ושש כיכר זהב, מלבד הכנסות נוספות מסוחרים, מלכים ופחות הארץ.
did_you_know.text_en: Did you know? The weight of the gold that came to Solomon in one year was 666 talents, not counting the additional revenues from merchants, kings, and the governors of the land.

did_you_know.text: הידעת? כיסא השנהב של שלמה היה מצופה זהב, ולצדו היו שש מעלות, אריות ליד הידיות ואריות נוספים על המעלות; הכתוב אומר שלא נעשה כמותו לכל ממלכה.
did_you_know.text_he: הידעת? כיסא השנהב של שלמה היה מצופה זהב, ולצדו היו שש מעלות, אריות ליד הידיות ואריות נוספים על המעלות; הכתוב אומר שלא נעשה כמותו לכל ממלכה.
did_you_know.text_en: Did you know? Solomon’s ivory throne was overlaid with gold. It had six steps, lions beside the armrests, and additional lions on the steps; the text says that no other kingdom had made anything like it.

did_you_know.text: הידעת? סוחרי המלך של שלמה הביאו את הסוסים ממצרים, והמרכבות והסוסים נמכרו גם למלכי החיתים ולמלכי ארם.
did_you_know.text_he: הידעת? סוחרי המלך של שלמה הביאו את הסוסים ממצרים, והמרכבות והסוסים נמכרו גם למלכי החיתים ולמלכי ארם.
did_you_know.text_en: Did you know? Solomon’s royal merchants brought horses from Egypt, and the chariots and horses were also sold to the kings of the Hittites and the kings of Aram.
